items.title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
items.summary: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer GLM 5.4 is now available from Chinese AI lab Z.ai. It's their first model to use a looped transformer architecture, which they describe like this: In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass. This gives us a deeper network without increasing the parameter count. This is the second mention of looped transformers I've seen in the past week - the first was Inkling 2 Mini from ...

items.title: Why cracking your knuckles doesn't cause arthritis
items.summary: Does cracking your knuckles cause arthritis? Dr. Donald Unger cracked only his left hand's knuckles for more than 60 years and kept the right as a control. Neither hand developed arthritis, and he won the 2009 Ig Nobel Prize in Medicine. In 2015, researchers filmed a knuckle crack in a real-time MRI and saw the crack come as a cavity formed in the joint. Sources: Ig Nobel Prize 2009 (Improbable Research); Kawchuk GN et al., "Real-Time Visualization of Joint Cavitation", PLOS ONE 10(4), 2015. Idea: AsapSCIENCE. Which knuckle do you crack first? #Shorts #health #science

items.title: Why you can't fold paper more than 7 times
items.summary: Why you can't fold paper more than 7 times. Seven folds is already 128 layers. In January 2002, high school junior Britney Gallivan folded a roll of toilet paper about 4,000 feet long 12 times. At 42 folds, 0.1 mm paper would be 439,805 km tall, past the Moon at 384,400 km. Sources: Guinness World Records (most times to fold a piece of paper), MathWorld "Folding", NASA Moon Fact Sheet. Idea: Hafu Go. Fold one yourself: how far do you get? #Shorts #math #science
